statement: Before the first 7-nut M8 drop the operator raised the brightness of the left and right LED fill lights and forgot to restore the original setting. This is NOT a confirmed change to camera exposure, gain, or gamma.
scope: Adds context only. Does not change the original NPZ, manifest, controller events, truth supplement, or previous analysis numbers.

relationship_to_previous_findings.interpretation: The over-bright LED fill lighting is a plausible contributor to the bright background, local glare, and the threshold anomaly that forced TH240 in the provisional replay. It is NOT established as the sole root cause.
alternatives_not_excluded: the scene illumination was too bright for the field exposure even after LED restoration
camera exposure/gain/gamma state at capture time is unknown: the capture tool neither set nor read the controls back

camera_controls_status.note: Current V4L2 readback (auto_exposure=1 manual, exposure_time_absolute=50, brightness=0, gamma=100, gain not exposed) is a snapshot taken after the run and does not prove the capture-time state. Do not assume the camera parameters were correct merely because the LED setting explains part of the overexposure.

counts_status.note: The 1200/2000 counts remain as recorded, but they must not be read as algorithm performance under normal lighting.

actions_paused: Do not adjust max_split_area based on this group.
Do not adjust max_missing, split thresholds, splitting algorithm, tracking logic, or PL design.
next_capture_requirements: First restore and fix the left and right LED brightness and angles; record the restored settings.
Verify the empty-baseline gray distribution and the material imaging under the restored lighting.
Separately set and read back the fixed camera controls (auto_exposure=1, exposure_time_absolute=50, brightness=0, gamma=100; gain not exposed by this UVC driver).
Require an empty-baseline gate result of PASS before drop_start; UNVERIFIED or FAIL blocks the cue.
